excluded_pilot: timing-icount0 used five compilations and serial compiler diagnostics; short windows were superseded by 50-compile cohorts with file-directed diagnostics.
interpretation: Stock/fork ordinary-RV64 pair isolates the fork difference for this pinned guest and these binaries; it is not a claim for all workloads.
Capstone/plain platform ratio includes different guest software/ABI, guest instruction volume and capability emulation. It cannot isolate per-instruction emulator cost or predict RTL slowdown.
Platform-plain is faster than fork-plain in this fixture. Machine/discovery/CPU settings differ, including x-pcrel=false; the cause is not isolated.
Removing icount reduces native GCC host CPU time in this experiment; no default changed and no whole-suite safety/timer qualification is inferred.
limitations: Only two samples per arm and mode on one host, one small repeated GCC test.
Timing markers include serial endpoint jitter and 100-Hz CPU accounting.
Existing binaries reused; scalar/native compiler provenance differs.
Same host build options include -O2 with debug symbols, no LTO, no TCG plugins loaded.
Remote host unavailable; measurements run locally on the CPU and affinity recorded in the cohorts.
QEMU fork pin unchanged; no emulator optimization or ISA semantic change implemented.
Host frequency and unrelated host activity not controlled; affinity and observed load recorded.
next_steps: Profile host execution of the native cohort separately from timings to rank helpers.
Isolate the PC-relative translation setting with a scalar control.
Qualify a no-icount fast functional-testing mode on timer/preemption and lifetime/race tests before changing test defaults.

evidence.note: Includes exact emulator binaries, build logs/options, commands, serial logs and timing reports; excludes duplicate stage files and guest disk images.
